what: Fifteen to 28 test runs ran at once and pushed the machine load to 148.
why: Every session ran validation on its own with no shared limit.
rule: Validation waits in the machine-wide queue.

what: Test runs kept going after the session that started them had died.
why: Nothing tied a running test to its parent session.
rule: A queue slot is reaped when its holder exits.

what: A session would not act on another session's relayed owner approval.
why: Nothing recorded the owner's own words, so the relay could not be checked.
rule: A relay record holds the owner's exact words, and production deploys, payments, credentials and the owner's rules files still need the owner's own message in the session that does them.

what: Two sessions built the same story (#692 and #693).
why: Nothing marked a story as taken before it was built.
rule: A story is claimed before it is built, and dispatch refuses a claimed story.

what: Sessions asked the owner questions in their own threads instead of through the manager.
why: Each session had no single place to send a question up.
rule: Owner questions go to the manager.

what: A change landed without full validation (#711).
why: The push happened before the repo's validation had passed.
rule: A push happens only after the repo's validation passes.

what: Installs were made against an owner rule when a new tool was added.
why: The install was judged on its own merit and the owner's rule that forbids it was not checked first.
rule: An install the owner's rules forbid is not made.

what: Designs did not mirror the market leaders.
why: The designs were built from the session's own taste, with no comparison against the best examples in the market.
rule: Before a design is built, the market leaders in its category are looked at and the design follows their proven structure.

what: Visuals were not checked frame by frame.
why: A visual was judged from one overview, so defects in single frames went unseen.
rule: A visual is checked frame by frame before it counts as done.
